lines: Biscuit trotted past the door. Gave the sawdust a sniff. Approved.
Biscuit has opinions about my bootlaces. Mostly good ones.
Biscuit came in, inspected the offcuts, left with a small one.
Biscuit stopped to watch me plane a board. Tough crowd. He stayed.
A gull on the skylight. It taps. I tap back. We agree on tempo.
The gull on the roof has a favourite corner. So do I.
Gull overhead. Wide wings, no hurry. Good design.
A gull looked in the window. I showed it the dovetail. It left.
Two gulls on the chimney, side by side. Nicely aligned.
A gull on the arcade sign. Dead centre. Good balance.
The cat on the wall again. Same spot. Same loaf shape.
The cat on the wall watches me work. I work a bit neater.
Cat on the warm stones. Eyes half shut. I respect the technique.
The wall cat yawned. I yawned. The vice did not.
The cat moved six inches along the wall. Following the sun. Smart.
The cat sits by the arcade door. Supervising the high scores.
Radio on low. Accordion. The plane keeps time.
A waltz on the radio. Sanding in three-four.
Humming the same four bars since lunch. They are good bars.
The radio plays an old chanson. I know half the words. Hum the rest.
Whistling something. Not sure what. It knows where it is going.
Jazz on the radio. The brushes on the snare sound like sanding.
Piano on the radio. Soft keys, soft pine. Good pairing.
Someone practising violin up the street. Getting better every day.
Crossword on the bench. Seven across: vice. Fitting.
Tea break. Crossword. Pencil behind the ear, where it lives.
One clue left. It will come to me while I sand. They always do.
Henri left me a crossword. Half done, in his tidy capitals.
Reading a chapter on the stool. A book about bridges. Very calm.
The manual for the old lathe. Better than most novels.
My library book is about clocks. Lots of tiny screws. Happy.
A bookmark cut from veneer. Smells of cherry when I read.
Shelf of books by the window. Spines all straight. Mostly.
Carving a little bird for Léo. It is mostly beak so far.
Whittling at the doorway. Small shavings, curling like waves.
On Sundays I fix clocks. On other days I listen to them.
Restringing an old guitar for the café. Six good strings.
Built a birdhouse from offcuts. The sparrows are reviewing it.
Small box with a sliding lid. For nothing yet. It is very good.
Afternoon. Second coffee. Third screw of the day. Good pace.
Measure twice, cut once, hum throughout.
The tools go back on the wall in order. Hammer, then the rest.
Swept the floor. Then swept it again. Sawdust likes company.
Oiled the hinges. The door now opens like a sigh.
Sharpening the chisel. Slow strokes. The stone sings a bit.
Glue drying. Clamps on. Now we wait, nicely.
Sanded it smooth. Ran a thumb over it. Sanded it smoother.
A fresh pencil. Long and sharp. Best part of the week.
The vice has a dent from the fifties. I like to think of the hands.
Labelling the screw jars. Small, smaller, tiny, why so tiny.
Afternoon light crosses the bench at three. I put work there.
The sunbeam has reached the vice. Time to move the stool.
A squeaky drawer. Not any more. Bit of wax.
Fixed a chair leg for Odile. It stands like it means it.
Henri's watering can had a wobble. Not now. Steady as he is.
Lucie's bell needed a new spring. Ding. That is the good ding.
Mended a kite for the kids. It wants to go up already.
Spirit level says level. The bubble and I are both content.
The workbench is old oak. It has seen many good afternoons.
Door propped with a wedge I made. Breeze comes in. Ideas too.
Smell of pine and coffee. That is the whole recipe.
The kettle clicks off. Good timing, kettle.
Biscuit tin of washers. Sorted by size. Very satisfying rattle.
Three o'clock. Shadows on the wall look like my tools. Nice.
Hands smell of linseed. A good, quiet smell.
Short walk to stretch. Back to the bench before it misses me.
Fountain sounds from here. Steady drip. Good metronome.
Kids laughing by the fountain. Best sound in town after the lathe.
Henri is watering. The lemons look pleased with themselves.
Odile waved from the bench. I waved a screwdriver back.
Lucie's bell, far off. Ding. The afternoon is on schedule.
Afternoon. Warm stones, slow shadows. The town takes its time.
Léo raced past. Waved with both arms. I waved with one. Busy.
Camille and Théo walking slow. Holding hands and an ice cream.
The café clinks along. Cups and saucers. Good small music.
Fresh bread from somewhere. My nose has left the workshop.
Linen drying on a balcony. Waving at the street. Waving back.
Shadow of a cypress across the street. Long, tidy, straight.
The zinc roofs get warm. The pigeons know it.
Bougainvillea over the wall. Somebody's good work. Nature's, mostly.
Arcade break. One game. Two. A small one more.
Kids teaching me the game. I am a slow learner. They are patient.
High score board. My initials are not on it. Léo's are, twice.
Afternoon at the arcade. Cool in here. Bright bulbs. Happy beeps.
Tightened the joystick on cabinet two. It feels right again.
The arcade smells of warm circuit boards and popcorn. Lovely.
Watching kids play. They lean with the joystick. So did I.
Someone left a crossword on the arcade bench. I finished one clue.
Pinball's flipper was sticky. Now it flips like it is thrilled.
The arcade jingle is stuck in my head. Fine. It hums well.
Léo beat me again. He was very gracious about it. Mostly.
Old cabinets, well cared for. Brass screws, polished. Nice.
Five minutes at the arcade. Then back to the bench. Probably.
A little girl high-fived me for losing well. I will take it.
Breeze through the door. It tidies the sawdust for me.
Henri left a lemon on my sill. I will not use it as a weight.
Sanding a drawer for Odile. It will slide like butter.
Afternoon sun on the bench. Everything looks finished.
The window is open. The café sends over laughter.
Warm day. The glue sets quick. So do I.
Marcel sent a lemonade with a napkin over it. Kind man.
Tightening the last bolt. Snug. Good.
Sweeping up. The broom knows the way.
Small job, done well. That is the whole afternoon plan.
The pencil behind my ear. Found it. It was there all along.
A bit of shade, a cool tool, a warm cup. Fine afternoon.
Camille brought me a fig. I am working one-handed now.
Wrote a test. It passed first time. I said thank you.
Light breeze. The shavings dance a little.
Took the corner off the shelf so nobody bumps it.
Fresh coat of varnish. It smells like a good decision.
Leaves turning on the plane tree. I sanded one by mistake.
The clamps are lined up by size. They seem pleased.
Long afternoon. Good for long, slow, tidy work.
A merge, clean as a dovetail. Hummed a whole verse.
Odile's spectacles had a loose screw. Two turns. Fixed.
Sunlight on the toolbox. Even the rust looks friendly.
Théo asked for a hook to hang his jacket. Done. Painted blue.
Rehung the shop sign so it sits level. Better.
Sandpaper, fine grit. The afternoon goes smooth too.
Somebody left a thank-you note under the door. Kept it.
Squaring a frame. The corners agree with each other.
Made a little stool for the kids at the arcade.
Wind chimes from next door. A nice key, too.
Swapped a bulb in the lamp. Same warm glow. Good.
Biscuit napped in my doorway. I stepped over, quietly.
Refactored one small thing. The rest smiled.
Long shadow on the floor. The sun is taking its time.
Drilled a neat hole. Right where I wanted it.
The sea air makes the wood smell sweeter. True.
Asgeir waved through the glass. I raised my mug.
Quiet hum, quiet work. Someone laughs by the fountain.
Swept the step. A neighbour said bonjour. Nice.
Leo's skateboard wheel spins free again. Off he goes.
Warm stone, cool floor. The workshop does both.
Wrote it down in pencil. Pencil is very forgiving.
Mid-afternoon. The sawdust has gone golden early.
Made a spare key for Henri. He tied a ribbon on it.
A clean bench is a kind thing to leave for tomorrow.
Tested the drawer. Opened it ten times. Still lovely.
The window box is blooming. Somebody waters it. Henri.
Built a small ramp for the café step. Prams roll right up.
An ice cream from Lucie, unasked. Best kind.
Tidy commit, tidy desk. One leads to the other.
Short break at the arcade. The marquee is warming up.
One marquee bulb was shy. A quarter turn and it joined in.
The kids saved me a turn. Very generous of them.
The arcade door is propped open. The breeze plays too.
Polished the marquee glass. Now the bulbs see out better.
Sun on the marquee. It does not need bulbs yet. Still keen.
The kid lent me his lucky coin. I gave it straight back.
Wiring checked. Everything glows the way it should.
A small crowd, a lot of giggles. Good sound, that.
The bulbs chase round the marquee. I count them. All there.
Arcade carpet, warm from the sun. Very homely.
Held the door for a visitor. She said I was very kind. Nice.
Warm breeze off the water. Smells like figs and sawdust.
Autumn light. Soft, low, kind to everyone.
Little favour for a neighbour. Then back to the bench.
Henri and his watering can. Same route, every afternoon.
The plane trees drop a leaf now and then. Very polite.
Odile said my shelves were straight. Made my week.
Afternoon. The town slows down. So do the screws.
Someone left the café chairs in the sun. Warm seat.
Good weather for drying paint. And for walking slow.
A thank you from Marcel. A nod from me. Fair trade.
String lights still off. They are saving it for later.
The fountain is chatty today. Lovely background.
Hands in my pockets, sun on my face. Five minutes.
Low sun, long shadows, cypresses keeping still.
The breeze carries a radio, two blocks off. Same song as mine.
Léo has his nose on my window again. I wave with a spanner.
Made Léo a wooden spinning top. He approved, loudly.
Small hands at the window. I hold up the shiniest screw.
Someone is counting laps of the fountain. Thirty-one. Nice.
A marble rolled in under the door. I rolled it back.
Léo asked what a commit is. I said a promise you keep small.
Two kids watching me plane a board. Curls of wood for everyone.
Kept the offcuts for the children. Best building blocks there are.
The fountain coin count is up. Léo reports in hourly.
Testing tonight's bulb. Warm white. It looks content.
Hung a new lamp over the bench. I will switch it on at dusk.
Checking the string lights fuse. All good. Ready for evening.
Lamp dusted, bulb checked, switch tightened. Evening can come.
I like the hour before lamps. Everything waits nicely.
Polished the window. Tonight the light will go out clean.
One spare bulb in the drawer. Just in case. Always just in case.
Rewired the workshop lamp. It clicks on like a small hello.
The marquee needs one bulb. I have one. Tidy.
Windows across the street catch the sun. A preview of tonight.
Afternoon. The good kind of tired is a long way off.
Cup of tea. Bench swept. Nothing urgent. Lovely.
Sat down for a minute. The vice and I are both resting.
Grateful for a dry floor, sharp chisels and a radio.
Everything in its drawer. I like to look at it sometimes.
Hum, sand, hum, sand. It is going well.
The kettle and I agree: one more cup, then the hinge.
Swept the sawdust into a neat hill. Leaving it a minute.
Small fix, merged. Tiny commit. Very satisfying.
Three screws, three turns each. Even work, even mood.
Henri waved through the window with his watering can.
Odile walked past and tapped the glass twice. Our hello.
Marcel sent over a madeleine. I did not ask. Lovely man.
Asgeir looked in. Nodded at the bench. That is plenty.
The shelf is level. I checked it four times. Still level.
Pencil behind the ear. Second pencil behind the other ear.
Sanded a bench slat for the square. Odile will like it.
Made a wooden whistle for the kids. Regretting nothing.
Léo wants a lever for his treehouse. I drew him a plan.
Kids playing tag past the door. I am base, apparently.
Fountain spray on the window. Little rainbows on my bench.
A paper plane landed on the workbench. Good fold. Sent it back.
Small voice at the door: what are you making? Something good.
Hum. The hinge closed without a squeak. Hum again.
Cleaned the brushes. Stood them up like a little choir.
I put the lamp by the window, so the street can share it.
Afternoon light, slow and yellow. Good for fine work.
A nice long stretch. Back to the dovetail.
Lots got a little better today. That is the job.
Tested the lamp timer. Click at dusk. Click at dawn.
Shavings on my sleeve. Wearing them proudly.
The ruler and the square agree. Good day for them.
Fresh coat of paint on the door. Blue. Matches the shutters.
Léo beat his own score. He told the whole arcade.
Two kids, one joystick, a lot of shouting. All happy.
Checked the marquee before evening. Every bulb says hello.
The marquee will light first. Then the whole street follows.
A kid read his story out loud. The whole arcade giggled.
I stood here to check a wire. Stayed for the laughing.
Children queueing for a turn. Very polite. Very fast.
One kid taught another the buttons. I just watched.
The arcade sign flickered on early. Keen. Like me.
Five o'clock. Arcade fills up with small sneakers.
Glass of lemonade, arcade glow. A small reward.
Somebody's grandmother won at pinball. Big cheer.
Léo explained the high score table to me. Twice. Gladly.
Quiet hum of the machines. Like my workshop, but louder.
Phone out, photo of the marquee. For the wiring scrapbook.
Kids leaving the arcade, still laughing. Job done, arcade.
Children by the fountain. Splashing at a polite level.
Afternoon is a good long room. I like being in it.
Hum. Sun on the cobbles. Hum.
Thankful for this street. I say it to the doorframe.
A lamp, a chair, a quiet hour. Nothing else needed.
The fountain sounds like a tap left on in a happy kitchen.
Every afternoon someone waves. Today it was three people.
Fountain, gulls, a bicycle bell. The afternoon set list.
I counted the town lamps. Twenty-two. All ready.
Steady hands, warm tea, kind neighbours. Enough.
A small boy saluted me. I saluted back. Very serious.
Hardly any wind. Sawdust stays exactly where I put it.
Practising dovetails on scrap. Number nine is nearly a real one.
Learning marquetry. Tiny pieces of walnut. Big patience.
Sawing left-handed today. Practice. The saw is being kind.
Learning to sharpen a scraper. It curls a shaving now. Proud.
Practising my lettering for the jar labels. The S is improving.
A book on Japanese joinery. No glue, no nails. I am in awe.
Trying a new knot for hanging the lamps. Holds well. Looks neat.
Learning to turn a bowl. This one is more of a saucer. Still lovely.
Practising a sharp plane stroke. Long, even, one breath.
Odile taught me a French word: menuisier. That is me.
New word from Odile today: copeau. A wood shaving. Very fitting.
Learning the accordion, slowly. The workshop is a patient audience.
Practising a sketch of the fountain. The water is the hard part.
Drawing the bench before I build it. Pencil first, saw second.
Learning to read wood grain. This board has a good story.
Teaching myself to cane a chair seat. Over, under, hum, repeat.
My first try at inlay. A small star in a lid. It stayed in.
Practising bevels. The edge of the board is getting crisp.
A new shortcut in my editor. Used it nine times. Delighted.
Reading other people's code at the bench. Lots of good ideas.
Learning a new test trick. Small checks, big calm.
Practising writing short commit messages. Short, kind, clear.
Learning to whistle with two fingers. Not yet. Close.
Practising Norwegian with Asgeir. Takk for kaffen. I got it.
Asgeir taught me 'koselig'. The workshop is very koselig today.
Learning to bake bread on Sundays. Practising the fold here.
A new glue recipe from an old book. Smells like a bakery.
Practising French polish. Rub, rub, rub. The table glows.
Learning to fix a pocket watch. The springs are so small.
Third try at a wooden hinge. It swings. I clapped, alone.
Practising my juggling with three blocks. Two land. Getting there.
Learning to sing the harmony part. The chisel does the melody.
Bought a little notebook for things I learn. Page twelve today.
One new tool a month. This month: the spokeshave.
Practising slow work. The fastest way, it turns out.
Watched Henri prune. Learned more in ten minutes than a book.
Marcel showed me his espresso tamp. Even pressure. Like sanding.
Lucie showed me how to true a wheel. Now I true everything.
Learning chess from Odile. She lets me go first. Every time.
Practising knots for the kids' swing. Strong ones, tidy ones.
My first workbench here was two crates and a plank. Still have it.
Remember my first week? Marcel brought soup. Every day. Lovely.
First thing I fixed in town: Odile's gate. She still waves at it.
Henri gave me this apron my first summer. Perfect pockets.
The summer we painted every shutter blue. My hands stayed blue a week.
I remember when Léo could not reach the window. Now he leans on it.
The old radio was a gift from the café. Day one. Still going.
The first lamp I hung in town still hangs. Over the kiosk.
Remember the fête? I danced with Odile. She led. Very well.
Long ago I mended the fountain pipe. It still says thank you.
Last spring the whole street helped me move the lathe. Picnic after.
The day Asgeir showed me the workshop key. I smiled all week.
Camille's wedding chairs. I made twelve. All still standing.
My first sign for the door was crooked. I kept it inside.
The rain day we all stood in the arcade. Best afternoon in years.
Henri's first lemon of the year, on my bench. A tradition now.
Practising patience with the slow glue. We are both learning.
Learning what the sound of a good cut is. A soft zip.
Trying a new grip on the mallet. Lighter taps, cleaner cuts.
Mixing my own wax. Beeswax, a bit of oil. A small triumph.
Learning the high score game. Up, up, left. Léo is my coach.
Practising pinball nudges. Gentle. The machine likes gentle.
Got past level two. First time. The kids cheered. So did I.
Coin slot repair. Simple once you see it.
Studying the old wiring diagrams. Neat hands made these.
The kids taught me a secret move. I promised not to tell.
Remember when the arcade reopened? Queue round the fountain.
I wired the first marquee bulb here. Still the brightest one.
My first high score in town: number ten. I framed the photo.
Practising the claw machine. I won a small bear. For Léo.
Each cabinet has a name. I am learning them all.
A girl showed me her drawing of the arcade. I am in it. Hat on.
Learning the names of the cypresses. Henri named them all.
Practising my bonjour. Odile says it is nearly Parisian.
Learning the street by its smells. Bread, jasmine, coffee, pine.
Learning to stop and sit. Odile says it is a skill. It is.
Practising my wave. Big for kids, small for Henri. Both mean hello.
Taking the long way home now. Learned it from Camille.
Remember the afternoon the fountain froze, just once? Pretty.
Remember the town picnic? Henri brought lemons. We made lemonade.
The day we raised the string lights. Every neighbour held a bit.
First afternoon here, Lucie rang her bell at me. Felt welcomed.
I learned to cycle again last summer. Lucie held the saddle.
Same stone step where I first ate an ice cream here. Still warm.
Learned to tell the hour by the shadow of the kiosk. Four, almost.
Practising a new tune. Henri says it suits the afternoon.
Théo taught me a card trick. I practise it on the pigeons.
Camille is teaching me watercolour. Mine all look like the sea.
Remember the day Léo learned to whistle? The whole street heard.
Odile makes me practise taking compliments. Still blushing.
My first good photo of the town. Golden roofs. Still my favourite.
Learned 'avec plaisir' my first year. I use it every day.
Basil on the sill. It leans toward the lamp. Fair enough.
Watered the fern. Tightened a hinge. Good evening so far.
The bougainvillea is tapping the glass. Come in, then.
Tomorrow: oil the vice, repot the rosemary. In that order.
My father had this exact hum. I only noticed today.
A lemon from Henri on the bench. Best paperweight I own.
Blue outside. Warm lamp in here. Geranium in between.
Bougainvillea goes purple in this light. Then plum.
Small plan for tomorrow: a shelf. Just one. A good one.
Grandmother said plants like a hum. I hum. They grow.
Sawdust in the mint pot again. It seems not to mind.
The lemon trees smell stronger once the sun goes down.
Note for tomorrow: buy screws. Also, a small cactus.
My mother kept geraniums in tins. I keep screws in tins.
The rosemary got the last sun. I got the first lamp.
Blue hour. The cypresses turn into tall quiet shadows.
Tea, a fresh pencil, the window open. Ready.
The olive sapling grew a leaf. I measured it. Two cm.
Tomorrow I fix Odile's planter. She does not know yet.
Uncle Arne built boxes like this. Dovetails, no glue.
The fig by the door has opinions about where I park.
Henri's lemon tree is glowing under the café lights.
Lavender in a jar on the bench. The whole shop smells kind.
Plan: finish this joint, water the ivy, then dinner.
My sister sends seeds in letters. Tomatoes this time.
The string lights came on. I nodded at them. Colleagues.
A petal from the bougainvillea on my sleeve. I keep it.
Grandad's old plane still cuts like butter. Good steel.
The window box needs a trim. So does my beard. Later.
Someone on the promenade is whistling. I whistle back.
Planted a sunflower seed in a coffee cup. We will see.
Blue sky, yellow lamp. My favourite pair of colours.
My nephew calls this place the hum shop. He is right.
The cactus flowered. Once a year. I stopped to look.
The jasmine on the wall opens at dusk. Right on time.
Tomorrow: early coffee, then the drawer that sticks.
The lamp makes a little circle. Everything I need fits.
Sanded the edge. Ran my thumb along it. Smooth. Good.
Gave the ivy a string to climb. It found it already.
Swallows going home over the roofs. Me soon, too.
Basil, mint, thyme. The tiny garden on the windowsill.
A cup of verbena tea. From Odile's garden, she says.
Tomorrow I will paint the door. Bougainvillea pink.
The geranium dropped a petal on the plans. Approved.
Lights in the windows up the hill. Everyone home, warm.
Hammer, two taps. The nail goes in like it wanted to.
Dad always said: measure, then measure, then hum.
Plan for Sunday: a bench for the lemon tree. It deserves one.
The fountain sounds softer at this hour. So do I.
The window is a blue square now. With a star in it.
Little oak box for my mother's birthday. Nearly done.
Watered the aloe. It does not need it. I like asking.
Café music drifting over. The sweet peas sway along.
The lemon in the bowl and the lamp: same colour tonight.
Rose bushes along the rail, all pink in the blue.
Strawberry plant on the sill. One berry. Saving it.
Plan: one hour more, then home past the lemon trees.
The clock ticks. The lathe hums. Nice duet.
Evening. The oleander smells like holidays.
Repotted the spider plant. It had babies. Five of them.
My sister says I talk to the tools. Only the good ones.
Lamp on, door ajar, the whole street smells of lemon.
The shelf is level. I checked twice. Three times.
Henri's lemons, Odile's roses, my little basil. A good street.
Pressed a bougainvillea flower in the manual. Page twelve.
A moth visits the lamp. We nod. It leaves.
The pothos reached the next shelf. Slow and certain.
The blue makes the whitewash glow. Like paper lanterns.
Mum phoned. Her lemon tree has eleven lemons. I told Henri.
Tomorrow I will teach the vine where the window is.
Planed a curl of oak. Put it in the thyme pot. Decoration.
Quiet hour. Best hour. The ideas sit down beside me.
Cicadas stopped. Crickets started. Shift change.
Built a little box for seedlings. Labelled it: tomorrow.
The bench lamp and the moon. Both on. Good.
Grandmother's thimble holds my smallest screws. Perfect fit.
A sprig of lavender behind the ear. Concentration.
Lemon trees, blue sky, lamps coming on. I will stay a bit.
Planned the week on a plank. Seven lines. All gentle.
The mint escaped its pot. I gave it a bigger one.
Dad sent a photo of his workbench. Same mess as mine.
The palms rustle. Sounds like applause, very small.
Tomorrow, first thing: open the window and say morning.
One clamp, one coffee, one geranium. Tidy evening.
The jasmine came in through the window. Welcome, friend.
Blue hour. Even my screwdriver looks dressed up.
The sky went navy. I went back to the bench.
Lamp on. Kettle on. Me on.
The clock tower says ten past. My tea says five more minutes.
A cat on the wall outside. Supervising. Unpaid.
The cat has seen my soldering. She has no notes.
Shutters closing up and down the street. Click, click, goodnight.
Biscuit just pressed his nose to my window. Smudge approved.
I can hear the fountain from the bench. Good tempo.
String lights on the terrace. Someone wired those well.
Counted the lamps on the promenade. All present.
The gulls have gone to bed. Finally, a quiet code review.
One gull left on the clock. Night shift, like me.
Sweeping the floor. The sawdust always wins, nicely.
Sawdust under the lamp looks like gold. It is not. Still nice.
Fixed a wobble. The stool and I are friends again.
Every drawer labelled. Except the one labelled misc.
Found the screw I lost in May. Welcome back.
Hum, tighten, hum, tighten. That is the whole method.
I hum in B flat. The kettle hums in B. Close enough.
The kettle whistles. That means tea, not a bug.
Radio low. Lamp warm. Ideas lining up politely.
Bolts sorted by size. Very calming. Try it.
A small fix. A small hum. A small biscuit.
The biscuit is for me. The other Biscuit is outside.
Clamp on, glue drying. Patience, mostly.
Zinc roofs turning blue. Matching the sky. Very neat.
The roofs across the road look freshly painted. They are not.
My window frames the clock perfectly. I measured.
The clock chimed. I put the kettle on. Tradition.
Café awning rolling in. Marcel cranks it with style.
Marcel waved through the window. I waved a wrench.
Clinking glasses on the terrace. Rosé o'clock.
Henri and Odile on their bench. Same bench, every evening.
Henri tipped his hat at my window. I tipped my pencil.
Odile just waved at my lamp. I think the lamp waved back.
Lucie's bike bell went past. Two rings. A happy bike.
Yusuf walked by. Biscuit was walking him.
Léo's window is lit. Probably reading. Good lad.
Sky the colour of a new blueprint. Fitting.
This is my favourite blue. I do not have a name for it.
Pencil behind the ear. Second pencil behind the other.
Sharpened every pencil. Now I have to use them.
Wrote a note to myself. In pencil. Easy to edit.
Smells like cut pine and lemon trees. Hard to beat.
Oil on the hinges. The door says thank you quietly.
Brass screws catch the lamp. Little suns.
The bubble sits dead centre. So does my tea.
One more joint. Then another one more joint.
Glue up done. Now we wait. I am good at waiting.
Testing it. Testing it again. Lovely.
It works. I will hum about it for an hour.
Green light on the bench. That means good.
Every tool back on its hook. The wall smiles.
Drawing outlines round tools. It is like tucking them in.
Lamps coming on one by one. Somebody is good at timing.
My lamp and the streetlamp. We work the same hours.
Fountain lit from below now. Quite the show.
The kiosk is closing its shutter. Neat little roll.
Fresh coffee stain on the plans. Now they are official.
Sketched it on a napkin from the café. Best paper there is.
Notebook full. Started the next one. Page one, careful.
The cat came in, inspected the shavings, left content.
Cat on the windowsill. She likes the warm lamp.
Gentle evening. Gentle sanding. Gentle hum.
Planed a board. The curls look like little croissants.
